name: North Dakota Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Knoephla, Steaks & Walleye
description:
North Dakota's restaurants, from a bowl of knoephla at Kroll's Diner to steaks in the Badlands and walleye in Grand Forks.

North Dakota Eats is a free guide to eating in North Dakota: 6 places for knoephla, fleischkuechle and kuchen and 5 for steaks and walleye that we checked by hand, plus 1,736 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 248 towns, from Fargo and Bismarck to Grand Forks, Minot, Williston and Medora. No account, no ads.

NORTH DAKOTA GUIDES
• Knoephla & Kuchen: German-Russian comfort food, from Kroll's Diner, Tasting Table's pick for the state's best diner, to Fargo's Wurst Bier Hall.
• Steaks & Walleye: Grand Forks steakhouses and walleye, Devils Lake's prime rib, and Medora's steaks, Pitchfork Steak Fondue included (seasonal).
• James Beard Honors: the restaurateurs behind Luna Fargo.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "knoephla", "kuchen", "walleye".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 story or a visitor bureau's own page or listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept only when the listing is high-confidence. North Dakota's inspection reports are search-only, so the app shows no inspection results and computes no grades; each place links to the state's page on who inspects where, and places on tribal lands are under tribal jurisdiction. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings. Newer restaurant data downloads from the North Dakota Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of North Dakota or its Department of Health and Human Services), any tribal nation, North Dakota Tourism or any visitor bureau, any university or team, or the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: North Dakota Eats is a free guide to restaurants in North Dakota (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: knoephla, fleischkuechle and kuchen, and steakhouses and walleye, 11 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 1,736 restaurants, cafés and bars in 248 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Knoephla & Kuchen (or Steaks & Walleye, James Beard Honors, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it. North Dakota publishes inspection reports only in search portals, so each place links to the state's page on who inspects where; the app shows no inspection results or grades.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("knoephla", "kuchen", "walleye").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside North Dakota (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on North Dakota, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "ND Eats" is the Home Screen name of "North Dakota Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the North Dakota Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and visitor-bureau pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/north-dakota-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers North Dakota; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution in the app.
